comparator.name: Interdisciplinary Social Science (Interdisciplinaire sociale wetenschap)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 curriculum establishes a 180-EC bachelor with a 135-EC major and 45-EC profiling space. The major comprises 75 EC of compulsory first- and second-year courses and 60 EC of major choices. Within those choices, 30 EC are fixed bachelor-research components: Literatuurstudie ISW (7.5 EC), Technieken voor analyse kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve gegevens (7.5 EC), and Bachelorproject ISW (15 EC). The remaining 30 EC are instantiated with the first four courses in the officially presented Social Policy and Public Health study path. Study paths are recommended, flexible groupings that may be combined or self-designed, not a compulsory named route, so route remains null. The 45-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

alternatives.concept: Integrates sociology, politics, psychology, empirical methods, policy and civic research to address complex social problems. It is the closest feasible UCR response to Utrecht’s broad interdisciplinary programme while acknowledging that UCR does not reproduce its prescribed interdisciplinary research sequence.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Relative to the broad programme, the curriculum adds a life-science foundation, epidemiology, medical and health psychology, psychodiagnostics and quantitative causal analysis. The organising question is how adolescents develop and respond to risk within cultural, digital and institutional contexts.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad interdisciplinary social-science response is feasible. The official Social Policy and Public Health and Youth Studies directions each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct additional programmes. Migration, Ethnic Relations and Multiculturalism is also independently evidenced, but production stops after the first two additional directions because three UCR alternatives is the permitted maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Sociology directly addresses social structures, inequality and the organisation of modern society, with different scope and credits.
Introduction to Brain & Behavior provides behavioural-science foundations, while the comparator integrates a broader range of psychological perspectives.
Qualitative Research Methodology directly addresses applied qualitative social research, with different scope and credits.
Modern Sociology develops theory connecting agency, structure and contemporary social problems, with different scope and credits.
Medical & Health Psychology directly studies health and wellbeing in social and behavioural context, with different scope and credits.
No single UCR course reproduces the comparator’s interdisciplinary introduction across its three thematic domains.
UCR combines disciplines across the curriculum but has no selected course devoted to comparing disciplinary and interdisciplinary knowledge.
UCR gender, psychology and sociology courses provide related perspectives, but no selected course reproduces the dedicated sexuality-and-society component.
Public Economics examines welfare, redistribution and policy responses, directly addressing a major part of the welfare-state course.
Comparative Public Policy directly develops policy analysis of social problems, though it lacks the comparator’s external-practice format.
UCR provides psychology, leadership and health courses, but no selected course directly integrates work, health and wellbeing.
Research Methods & Statistics directly addresses introductory research design and statistics, with broader cross-disciplinary scope.
Statistics & Experimental Methods addresses advanced quantitative analysis, while the comparator combines quantitative and qualitative processing.
UCR has no selected compulsory group learning-research project equivalent to Leeronderzoek ISW.
The compulsory individual ISW literature study has no direct selected UCR counterpart.
UCR methods courses are aligned elsewhere; no additional selected course reproduces this separate final qualitative/quantitative analysis component.
UCR’s optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against the compulsory 15-EC Bachelorproject; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR programme.
The genuine 45-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a particular minor, exchange, internship or elective package.

notes.text: Utrecht’s programme integrates sociology, psychology, pedagogy and cultural anthropology through a prescribed interdisciplinary and research-methods sequence, flexible thematic study paths and a 30-EC bachelor-research package. UCR can combine substantial social theory, politics, psychology, research, policy, youth, health and media study, but distributes these subjects across disciplines rather than reproducing the same structured ISW sequence.
